def: The French first-instance court that decides individual disputes between employers and employees.

formal.ex: Any dispute arising out of this contract shall be referred to [[the French employment tribunal]].
formal.ex_us: Any dispute arising out of this contract shall be referred to [[the French labor court]].

everyday.ex: If she takes this to [[the employment tribunal]], we need to be able to show our reasons.
everyday.ex_us: If she takes this to [[the labor court]], we need to be able to show our reasons.

collocations: to go before the employment tribunal
to be heard by the labor court
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, l'« Employment Tribunal » existe réellement : précisez « the French employment tribunal » pour éviter la confusion. Aux États-Unis, il n'y a pas de juridiction du travail : les litiges vont devant les tribunaux ordinaires (« state or federal court ») ou en arbitrage ; « labor court » y est une traduction, pas une institution.

explain.written: The conseil de prud'hommes is the French first-instance employment court; it is composed of equal numbers of lay judges drawn from employers and from employees, and has exclusive jurisdiction over individual employment disputes.
explain.spoken: The conseil de prud'hommes is our employment tribunal - the twist is that the judges aren't professional judges, they're people from the employers' side and the employees' side, in equal numbers.

def: A judge who is not a career judge but an employer or an employee appointed to sit on the French employment tribunal.

formal.ex: The panel is composed of four [[lay judges]], two representing employers and two representing employees.

everyday.ex: Bear in mind that you'll be in front of [[non-professional judges]], so keep the argument practical.

note_fr: « Lay » signifie ici « non professionnel » (comme dans « layman »). Ne traduisez pas « conseiller » par « counsellor » ni « adviser » : il s'agit bien d'un juge. Au Royaume-Uni, les « lay members » peuvent siéger aux côtés d'un juge professionnel ; en France, il n'y a aucun magistrat de carrière en première instance, sauf départage.

explain.written: Conseillers prud'homaux are lay judges, appointed on the nomination of trade unions and employers' organisations, who sit in equal numbers on the French employment tribunal.
explain.spoken: The judges are lay people - half come from the employers' side, half from the unions' side. There's no professional judge unless they can't agree.

def: To start legal proceedings by formally asking a court or tribunal to decide a dispute.

formal.ex: The Employee [[brought proceedings against]] the Company before the Paris employment tribunal.
formal.ex_us: The Employee [[filed suit against]] the Company before the Paris labor court.

everyday.ex: He has twelve months to [[bring a claim against]] us if he wants to challenge the dismissal.
everyday.ex_us: He has twelve months to [[file a claim against]] us if he wants to challenge the termination.

informal.ex: She's threatening to [[take us to tribunal]] over the bonus.
informal.ex_us: She's threatening to [[take us to court]] over the bonus.

collocations: to bring a claim for unfair dismissal
to lodge a claim with the tribunal
to file a claim in court
note_fr: « Saisir » ne se traduit ni par « seize » (= saisir un bien) ni par « seise ». Le Britannique dit « to bring / lodge / issue a claim », l'Américain « to file a claim / a lawsuit ». « To take someone to tribunal » s'emploie sans article au Royaume-Uni.

def: The process of resolving employment disputes through a court or tribunal.

formal.ex: The Company wishes to avoid the cost and uncertainty of [[litigation]].

everyday.ex: We've got [[a legal dispute]] with a former sales manager that's been running for two years.

collocations: to be involved in a dispute
note_fr: « Litigation » est indénombrable : on ne dit pas « a litigation » mais « a dispute », « a case », « a claim ». « Contentious » est un adjectif (« a contentious issue » = un sujet qui fâche), jamais un nom. « Litigious » qualifie une personne procédurière.

def: The person who starts a legal claim against someone else.

formal.ex: [[The Claimant]] seeks damages for unfair dismissal and payment of outstanding overtime.
formal.ex_us: [[The Plaintiff]] seeks damages for wrongful termination and payment of unpaid overtime.

everyday.ex: In nine cases out of ten, [[the claimant]] is the employee.
everyday.ex_us: In nine cases out of ten, [[the plaintiff]] is the employee.

note_fr: En Angleterre, on dit « claimant » (le mot « plaintiff » y a été abandonné dans la procédure civile) ; aux États-Unis, « plaintiff » devant les tribunaux et « claimant » en arbitrage. N'employez pas « demander » ni « applicant », qui désigne plutôt un candidat ou l'auteur d'une requête particulière.

def: The person or company against whom a legal claim is brought.

formal.ex: [[The Respondent]] denies that the dismissal was unfair.
formal.ex_us: [[The Defendant]] denies that the termination was wrongful.

everyday.ex: As [[the respondent]], the company gets the claim form and then has to reply in writing.
everyday.ex_us: As [[the defendant]], the company gets the complaint and then has to reply in writing.

collocations: to be named as a respondent
to be named as a defendant
note_fr: Devant l'Employment Tribunal britannique, l'employeur est « the respondent » ; devant les tribunaux civils anglais et américains, « the defendant ». Aux États-Unis, « respondent » s'emploie en arbitrage et en appel. Attention à l'orthographe : « defendant », avec un a.

def: To be the party against whom an employee has started legal proceedings.

formal.uk: to be the subject of proceedings
formal.us: to be the subject of a lawsuit
formal.ex: The Company is currently [[the subject of proceedings]] brought by three former employees.
formal.ex_us: The Company is currently [[the subject of a lawsuit]] brought by three former employees.

everyday.ex: If we skip the meeting, we could [[face a tribunal claim]] within weeks.
everyday.ex_us: If we skip the meeting, we could [[face a lawsuit]] within weeks.

informal.ex: Nobody wants to [[get taken to tribunal]] over a missing signature.
informal.ex_us: Nobody wants to [[get sued]] over a missing signature.

collocations: to be on the receiving end of a claim
to be hit with a lawsuit
note_fr: N'employez pas « to be attacked », qui évoque une agression physique. L'employeur « faces a claim » puis « defends the claim ». « To be hit with a lawsuit » est familier et surtout américain.

def: To start a court case against a person or organisation in order to obtain money or another remedy.

formal.ex: The Employee reserves the right to [[take legal action against]] the Company.

everyday.ex: He's [[suing]] his former employer for unpaid commission.

note_fr: « To sue » est transitif direct : « to sue the company », jamais « to sue against ». On « sues for » une somme ou un motif. Le verbe est très courant aux États-Unis ; pour l'Employment Tribunal, un Britannique dira plus volontiers « to bring a claim ». « To pursue » signifie poursuivre un objectif, pas poursuivre en justice ; « to prosecute » relève du pénal.

def: A dispute that has been brought before a court or tribunal for decision.

formal.ex: The parties agree to keep the existence of [[the proceedings]] confidential.

everyday.ex: [[The case]] is unlikely to be heard before next autumn.
everyday.ex_us: [[The lawsuit]] is unlikely to be heard before next fall.

note_fr: Faux ami majeur : « process » n'est pas un procès. « Trial » désigne l'audience au fond devant un juge ou un jury (surtout aux États-Unis et au pénal) ; pour une affaire prud'homale, préférez « case », « claim » ou « proceedings » (toujours au pluriel dans ce sens).

def: A qualified professional who advises clients on the law and represents them in legal proceedings.

formal.ex: The Employee was assisted throughout by [[legal counsel]].
formal.ex_us: The Employee was assisted throughout by [[counsel]].

everyday.ex: Has he already instructed a [[lawyer]]?
everyday.ex_us: Has he already retained an [[attorney]]?

note_fr: « Advocate » est un faux ami : en anglais courant, c'est un défenseur d'une cause (sauf en Écosse). En France, la profession est unique ; en Angleterre, elle se divise entre « solicitor » et « barrister ». « Lawyer » est le terme générique partout ; « attorney » est américain. « Counsel » est invariable et sans article : « counsel for the employer ».

def: A lawyer who specialises in presenting cases orally before courts and tribunals.

formal.ex: The Respondent was represented at the hearing by [[counsel]].
formal.ex_us: The Defendant was represented at the hearing by [[trial counsel]].

everyday.ex: Our solicitors have brought in a [[barrister]] for the three-day hearing.
everyday.ex_us: Our firm has brought in a [[trial lawyer]] for the three-day hearing.

note_fr: En Angleterre, le « solicitor » conseille le client, prépare le dossier et correspond avec la partie adverse ; le « barrister » (qu'on appelle « counsel ») plaide à l'audience, sur instruction du solicitor. L'avocat français fait les deux. Aux États-Unis, la profession est unique : « attorney », et « litigator » ou « trial lawyer » pour celui qui plaide.

def: A lawyer employed by a company to advise it, as opposed to one working in a law firm.

formal.ex: All correspondence with the tribunal must be approved by [[in-house counsel]].

everyday.ex: Run it past the [[in-house lawyer]] before you reply to his solicitor.
everyday.ex_us: Run it by [[in-house counsel]] before you reply to his attorney.

note_fr: Ne traduisez pas « juriste » par « jurist », qui désigne un théoricien du droit. Le directeur juridique est le « General Counsel » (GC) ou « Head of Legal ». Différence de fond : au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, le juriste d'entreprise est en principe un avocat à part entière dont les avis bénéficient du secret professionnel ; en France, sa situation est différente.

def: To speak and act for a party in legal proceedings.

formal.ex: We [[act on behalf of]] Ms Dupont in connection with her dismissal.

everyday.ex: Which firm is [[acting for]] the employee?
everyday.ex_us: Which firm is [[representing]] the employee?

note_fr: Devant le conseil de prud'hommes, l'avocat n'est pas obligatoire en première instance : une partie peut se défendre seule (« to represent oneself » ; au Royaume-Uni « a litigant in person », aux États-Unis « to appear pro se »). En français on distingue « assister » et « représenter » ; l'anglais dit « represent » dans les deux cas. Jamais « to assist » pour « assister à ».

def: A person listed by an administrative authority, on a union's or employers' organisation's proposal, who may represent a party before the French employment courts instead of a lawyer.

formal.ex: The Claimant was represented on appeal by [[an accredited union representative]] rather than by a lawyer.

everyday.ex: She can't afford a lawyer, so [[a union rep]] is handling her case.

collocations: to be represented by a union official
note_fr: Notion française : le défenseur syndical peut représenter le salarié (ou l'employeur) devant le conseil de prud'hommes et la cour d'appel en matière prud'homale. Au Royaume-Uni, un « trade union official » peut aussi accompagner ou représenter un salarié devant le tribunal ; aux États-Unis, la représentation en justice est réservée aux avocats.

explain.written: A défenseur syndical is a union-nominated, officially listed lay representative who is entitled to assist or represent a party before the French employment tribunal and, in employment matters, before the court of appeal.
explain.spoken: In France you don't need a lawyer for this - an approved union representative can run the case for you, even on appeal.

def: The two-member panel of the French employment tribunal that first tries to bring the parties to an agreement and, failing that, organises the next steps of the case.

formal.ex: The matter was first listed before [[the conciliation and case-management panel]], composed of one employer judge and one employee judge.

everyday.ex: Nothing gets decided at [[the conciliation panel]] - it's there to see whether the two sides can settle.

collocations: to be listed before the conciliation panel
to set a timetable for the case
to refer the case to a full hearing
note_fr: N'essayez pas de traduire mot à mot (« office of conciliation and orientation » ne veut rien dire). Dites « conciliation panel » et expliquez son double rôle : tenter la conciliation, puis fixer le calendrier d'échange des pièces et des conclusions. Au Royaume-Uni, la conciliation se fait avant la saisine, par l'intermédiaire d'Acas, et non devant les juges.

explain.written: The bureau de conciliation et d'orientation is the first stage of French employment tribunal proceedings: a panel of one employer judge and one employee judge attempts to conciliate the parties and, if no agreement is reached, sets the timetable for the case.
explain.spoken: The first stage is a short session in front of two judges, one from each side, who try to get the parties to settle. If that fails, they set the dates for the rest of the case.

def: A first, short, private hearing at which the judges try to help the parties reach an agreement.

formal.ex: The parties are required to attend the [[conciliation hearing]] in person or to be duly represented.

everyday.ex: Most cases don't settle at the [[conciliation stage]], but it's worth going in with a figure in mind.

collocations: to reach an agreement at conciliation
note_fr: « Conciliation » existe en anglais et convient parfaitement ; évitez « reconciliation », qui s'emploie pour des personnes qui se réconcilient ou pour un rapprochement comptable. L'audience de conciliation n'est pas publique : dites « held in private ». Aux États-Unis, l'équivalent fonctionnel le plus proche est la « mediation » ou la « settlement conference ».

def: The hearing at which the court listens to both sides' arguments on the merits before deciding the case.

formal.ex: The case has been listed for [[the hearing on the merits]] before a panel of four judges.
formal.ex_us: The case has been set for [[the trial on the merits]] before a panel of four judges.

everyday.ex: We won't get to [[the full hearing]] for at least a year.
everyday.ex_us: We won't get to [[the trial]] for at least a year.

collocations: to go to a full hearing
note_fr: Le « bureau de jugement » se rend par « the judgment panel » : deux conseillers employeurs et deux conseillers salariés. Au Royaume-Uni, on parle de « full hearing » ou « final hearing » ; « trial » est réservé aux tribunaux civils et pénaux. Aux États-Unis, « trial » est le terme normal, souvent devant un jury. « On the merits » = au fond.

def: A situation in which the judges are equally divided, so that no majority decision can be reached.

formal.ex: In the event of [[an equality of votes]], the case is reheard under the chairmanship of a professional judge.
formal.ex_us: In the event of [[an evenly divided vote]], the case is reheard with a professional judge presiding.

everyday.ex: With two judges from each side, [[a split decision]] is always a possibility.

informal.ex: If it ends in [[a deadlock]], add another year to the timetable.

note_fr: Le partage de voix est propre à la composition paritaire du conseil de prud'hommes (deux contre deux). Ne dites pas « sharing of voices ». « Tie » appartient aussi au vocabulaire sportif (match nul), ce qui rend l'image très parlante pour un interlocuteur anglophone.

def: A professional judge who is called in to preside over a new hearing when the lay judges of the French employment tribunal are evenly divided.

formal.ex: The case was referred to [[the tie-breaking judge]], a professional judge of the local civil court.

everyday.uk: a professional judge to break the tie
everyday.us: a professional judge to break the tie
everyday.ex: The panel couldn't agree, so they've called in [[a professional judge to break the tie]].

collocations: to be referred to the tie-breaking judge
note_fr: Notion française sans équivalent. Au Royaume-Uni, l'idée voisine est celle de « casting vote » (voix prépondérante d'un président), mais ce n'est pas le même mécanisme : en France, l'affaire est replaidée devant la formation complétée par un magistrat professionnel. Signalez toujours l'allongement des délais que cela entraîne.

explain.written: Where the four lay judges are evenly divided, the case is reheard by the same panel presided over by a professional judge, known as the juge départiteur, whose participation makes a majority decision possible.
explain.spoken: If the four judges split two-two, the case is heard again with a professional judge in the chair to break the tie. It's called départage, and it adds months to the process.

def: A meeting of a court or tribunal at which the parties present their case to the judges.

formal.ex: The [[hearing]] will take place on 12 March at 9.00 am.

everyday.ex: How long is the [[hearing]] likely to last - an hour, a whole day?

note_fr: Faux ami : « audience » désigne le public d'un spectacle ou d'une conférence, jamais une audience de tribunal. À huis clos = « in private » (UK) ou « in closed session » ; en audience publique = « in open court ». Ne confondez pas avec le « disciplinary hearing », qui est l'entretien préalable à l'anglaise.

def: The official document telling a party when and where the hearing will take place.

formal.ex: The Respondent received [[notice of hearing]] by registered post on 3 May.

everyday.ex: Has [[the hearing notice]] come through yet? I need to block the date.

collocations: to be given notice of the hearing
note_fr: « Convocation » en anglais désigne une cérémonie universitaire ou une assemblée religieuse : à proscrire. « Summons » (singulier malgré le s ; pluriel « summonses ») est plus solennel et, aux États-Unis, désigne l'acte qui accompagne la « complaint ». « To convoke » est rarissime ; dites « to summon » ou « to call ».

def: To be physically present at the court or tribunal on the day of the hearing.

formal.ex: The parties shall [[appear before]] the tribunal in person or through their representatives.

everyday.ex: Does the HR director need to [[attend the hearing]], or can the lawyer go alone?

note_fr: « Assister à » = « to attend » ; « to assist » veut dire aider. « To appear » est le verbe juridique (d'où « appearance »). L'absence se dit « failure to attend » ou « non-appearance », pas « absence at the audience ».

def: A decision to move a hearing to a later date.

formal.ex: The tribunal [[adjourned the hearing]] to allow the Respondent to reply to the new evidence.
formal.ex_us: The court [[continued the hearing]] to allow the Defendant to reply to the new evidence.

everyday.ex: The other side has asked to [[postpone the hearing]] again.

informal.ex: They've [[pushed the hearing back]] to June.

note_fr: Piège américain : « to continue a hearing » signifie la reporter, et non la poursuivre ; « continuance » = renvoi. Ne traduisez pas « renvoi » par « return » ni « dismissal ». « To adjourn » peut aussi signifier simplement suspendre la séance (« adjourned for lunch »).

def: To present a party's arguments orally to the judges.

formal.ex: Counsel for each party will have twenty minutes to [[make oral submissions]].
formal.ex_us: Counsel for each party will have twenty minutes to [[present oral argument]].

everyday.ex: Who's going to [[argue the case]] on the day - the partner or her associate?

collocations: to argue that the dismissal was fair
note_fr: « To plead » n'est pas « plaider » : il signifie surtout exposer ses prétentions par écrit (« pleadings ») ou, au pénal, « to plead guilty ». « To argue » n'implique aucune dispute : c'est simplement argumenter. La plaidoirie finale est « closing submissions » (UK) ou « closing argument » (US).

def: To be likely to win because the facts, the evidence and the law are on one's side.

formal.uk: to have good prospects of success
formal.us: to have a strong likelihood of success
formal.ex: In our opinion, the Company [[has good prospects of success]] on the overtime claim.
formal.ex_us: In our opinion, the Company [[has a strong likelihood of success]] on the overtime claim.

everyday.ex: Honestly, I think she [[has a strong case]] - there's nothing in writing on our side.

informal.ex: Without the appraisals, we're [[on shaky ground]].

note_fr: « Dossier » existe en anglais mais désigne un dossier de renseignements sur quelqu'un : ici, dites « case ». « Prospects of success » est la formule de l'avocat britannique ; un pourcentage se dit « a 60% chance of succeeding ». « The merits » = le fond, le bien-fondé.

def: The document that starts the proceedings by setting out who is claiming what, and on what grounds.

formal.ex: [[The claim form]] must set out a summary of the grounds for each claim and list the supporting documents.
formal.ex_us: [[The complaint]] must set out a summary of the grounds for each claim and list the supporting documents.

everyday.ex: We received [[the claim]] on Monday - he's asking for eighteen months' salary.
everyday.ex_us: We received [[the complaint]] on Monday - he's asking for eighteen months' salary.

collocations: to be served with a complaint
note_fr: Piège : au Royaume-Uni, « a complaint » est une simple réclamation (interne ou commerciale) ; aux États-Unis, c'est l'acte introductif d'instance. « Request » ne convient pas. Devant l'Employment Tribunal, le formulaire de saisine s'appelle l'« ET1 » et la réponse de l'employeur l'« ET3 ».

def: The document in which a party's lawyer sets out the facts, the legal arguments and what the court is asked to order.

formal.ex: The Respondent shall file its [[written submissions]] no later than 15 September.
formal.ex_us: The Defendant shall file its [[brief]] no later than September 15.

everyday.ex: Their [[submissions]] came in last night - forty pages, mostly about the bonus.
everyday.ex_us: Their [[brief]] came in last night - forty pages, mostly about the bonus.

note_fr: Faux ami : « conclusions » en anglais ne désigne que la fin d'un raisonnement. Second piège : au Royaume-Uni, « a brief » est le dossier qu'un solicitor remet au barrister, alors qu'aux États-Unis c'est le mémoire déposé au tribunal. « Pleadings » désigne les actes qui fixent les prétentions (claim, defence), pas l'argumentation développée.

def: Each separate item that a claimant asks the court to award or decide.

formal.ex: The tribunal dismissed every [[head of claim]] save that relating to unpaid overtime.
formal.ex_us: The court dismissed every [[claim for relief]] except the one relating to unpaid overtime.

everyday.ex: The biggest [[part of the claim]] is the overtime, not the dismissal.

note_fr: « Chef » ne se traduit pas par « chief ». Le chiffrage des demandes est, au Royaume-Uni, le « schedule of loss » ; aux États-Unis, les fondements juridiques invoqués dans la « complaint » sont des « counts » ou « causes of action ». « Demand » est un faux ami : c'est une exigence, une sommation.

def: A claim made by the defending party against the person who started the proceedings, in the same case.

formal.ex: The Company [[brought a counterclaim]] for repayment of the training costs.
formal.ex_us: The Company [[filed a counterclaim]] for repayment of the training costs.

everyday.ex: We could [[counterclaim]] for the laptop and the unreturned advance, but is it worth it?

collocations: a counterclaim for breach of the non-compete
note_fr: Aucun rapport avec « reconvention ». « Counterclaim » est à la fois nom et verbe. En pratique, l'employeur français forme surtout des demandes reconventionnelles pour procédure abusive ou au titre des frais de procédure ; expliquez-le, car un client américain s'attend parfois à des contre-attaques plus larges.

def: A formal letter, usually from a lawyer, requiring the other party to pay or act within a set time, failing which proceedings will be started.

formal.ex: By a [[letter before claim]] dated 4 April, the Employee's solicitors demanded payment of the outstanding bonus.
formal.ex_us: By a [[demand letter]] dated April 4, the Employee's attorneys demanded payment of the outstanding bonus.

everyday.ex: We've had a [[solicitor's letter]] giving us fourteen days to pay.
everyday.ex_us: We've had a [[letter from his attorney]] giving us fourteen days to pay.

collocations: to send a letter before claim
to give formal notice to pay
note_fr: Pas de « letter of formal demand » calquée sur le français dans un contexte britannique : la formule consacrée est « letter before claim » (ou « letter before action »). « To put someone on notice » = aviser formellement quelqu'un, le mettre en demeure. Aux États-Unis, « demand letter » est le terme usuel.

def: To deliver a legal document to a party officially, in the way the rules require.

formal.ex: The time limit for appeal runs from the date on which [[the judgment was served on]] the parties.

everyday.ex: We [[were served with]] the claim last week, so the clock is already running.

collocations: to serve a document on someone
note_fr: Construction : « to serve a document on someone » ou « to serve someone with a document ». « To signify » veut dire signifier au sens de « vouloir dire ». « To notify » existe mais se construit « to notify someone of something », jamais « to notify a decision to someone ».

def: The period within which a step in the proceedings must be taken, or the date by which it must be done.

formal.ex: The appeal was not lodged [[within the prescribed time limit]] and is therefore inadmissible.
formal.ex_us: The appeal was not filed [[within the prescribed deadline]] and is therefore inadmissible.

everyday.ex: What's the [[deadline]] for sending our documents to the other side?

note_fr: Faux ami classique : « delay » signifie retard, jamais délai. « Dans un délai d'un mois » = « within one month ». Le point de départ se dit « time runs from... ». Proroger un délai : « to extend the time limit », « to grant an extension ».

def: The period fixed by law after which a claim can no longer be brought.

formal.ex: The [[limitation period]] for a claim relating to termination of the contract is twelve months from notification of the dismissal.
formal.ex_us: The [[statute of limitations]] for a claim relating to termination of the contract is twelve months from notification of the dismissal.

everyday.uk: time limit for bringing a claim
everyday.us: time limit for filing a claim
everyday.ex: The [[time limit for bringing a claim]] is much shorter in the UK than in France.
everyday.ex_us: The [[time limit for filing a claim]] varies a lot from one state to another.

collocations: the statute of limitations has run
note_fr: « Prescription » en anglais est une ordonnance médicale : faux ami absolu. En France, les délais varient selon l'objet de la demande (rupture du contrat, exécution du contrat, salaires). Au Royaume-Uni, le délai pour saisir l'Employment Tribunal est très bref, de l'ordre de quelques mois : vérifiez toujours la règle en vigueur. Aux États-Unis, il dépend de la loi invoquée et de l'État.

def: No longer able to be brought before a court because the legal time limit has passed.

formal.ex: The claim for arrears of salary relating to the earlier period is [[time-barred]].

everyday.ex: Anything before 2022 is [[out of time]], so that knocks a third off the claim.
everyday.ex_us: Anything before 2022 is [[too late to file]], so that knocks a third off the claim.

collocations: to bring a claim in time
to be barred by the statute of limitations
note_fr: Ne dites jamais « prescribed » : « prescribed by law » signifie « prévu, imposé par la loi », soit l'inverse d'une action éteinte. Variante britannique : « statute-barred ». Une demande formée à temps est « in time ».

def: The court's organisation of the steps and dates by which the parties must exchange arguments and evidence so that the case is ready to be heard.

formal.ex: The panel issued [[case management directions]] fixing the dates for the exchange of submissions and exhibits.
formal.ex_us: The court issued [[a scheduling order]] fixing the dates for the exchange of briefs and exhibits.

everyday.ex: Under [[the timetable]], we file in June and they reply in September.
everyday.ex_us: Under [[the schedule]], we file in June and they reply in September.

note_fr: Ne traduisez pas littéralement (« putting in state »). Au Royaume-Uni, le tribunal donne des « directions » ou « case management orders », souvent lors d'une « preliminary hearing » ; aux États-Unis, c'est le « scheduling order ». Devant le conseil de prud'hommes, ce rôle revient au bureau de conciliation et d'orientation.

def: The documents, statements and other material used to show the court that a fact is true.

formal.ex: The Company has produced no [[evidence]] that the Employee was warned about his performance.

everyday.ex: Do we have any [[proof]] that she actually received the letter?

note_fr: « Evidence » est indénombrable : jamais « an evidence » ni « evidences » ; dites « a piece of evidence », « some evidence ». Ne le confondez pas avec « évidence » (= « something obvious »). « Proof » est plus fort (la preuve décisive) ; « a proof » est une épreuve d'imprimerie.

def: A document or object formally produced to the court as evidence, usually numbered.

formal.ex: The warning letter of 3 March is produced as [[Exhibit]] 12.

everyday.ex: Which [[document]] shows the bonus was agreed - is it the email from June?

collocations: to produce a document as an exhibit
note_fr: « Piece » ne convient pas (sauf dans « a piece of evidence »). Le bordereau de pièces est « the list of exhibits ». Devant l'Employment Tribunal britannique, les documents des deux parties sont réunis dans un dossier commun paginé, le « bundle », et l'on cite la page plutôt qu'un numéro de pièce.

def: To give the other party copies of the documents on which one relies, or which one is required to hand over.

formal.ex: Each party shall [[disclose]] its exhibits to the other party in good time before the hearing.
formal.ex_us: Each party shall [[produce]] its exhibits to the other party in good time before the hearing.

everyday.ex: They still haven't [[sent over]] their documents, and the hearing is in three weeks.

informal.ex: We'll have to [[hand over]] the emails sooner or later.

collocations: to disclose a document to the other side
note_fr: « To communicate documents » est un calque : on « discloses », « produces » ou « exchanges » des pièces. Différence de fond : en France, chaque partie communique les pièces qu'elle choisit d'invoquer ; dans les pays de common law, elle doit en principe aussi révéler les documents pertinents qui lui sont défavorables.

def: The stage of common-law proceedings in which each party must reveal to the other the relevant documents and information it holds, including those that harm its own case.

formal.ex: The parties shall give [[disclosure]] of all documents relevant to the issues by 1 June.
formal.ex_us: The parties shall complete [[discovery]] of all documents relevant to the issues by June 1.

everyday.ex: Be careful what you put in an email - it could all come out in [[disclosure]].
everyday.ex_us: Be careful what you put in an email - it could all come out in [[discovery]].

note_fr: Rien de comparable en France, où le juge peut seulement ordonner la production de pièces déterminées. La « discovery » américaine est beaucoup plus large (documents, courriels, interrogatoires écrits, dépositions) et très coûteuse ; la « disclosure » anglaise est plus encadrée. Conséquence pratique à rappeler aux managers : tout écrit interne peut finir devant le juge.

def: In US litigation, the questioning of a witness under oath by the lawyers before trial, recorded word for word.

formal.ex: Plaintiff's counsel intends to [[take the deposition of]] the HR Director and two line managers.

everyday.ex: You may [[be deposed]], which means a full day of questions from the other side's lawyer.

collocations: to prepare a witness for deposition
note_fr: Procédure typiquement américaine, inconnue en France et pratiquement absente au Royaume-Uni. Elle se déroule dans un cabinet d'avocats, sans juge, mais sous serment. « To depose » n'a ici rien à voir avec « destituer ». Un DRH français d'une filiale de groupe américain peut y être convoqué : il faut le préparer.

fr: obligation de conservation des documents en vue d'un litige
def: An instruction not to delete or destroy any document that may be relevant to a dispute that has started or is expected.

formal.ex: The Legal Department has issued [[a document preservation notice]] covering all correspondence relating to the Employee.
formal.ex_us: The Legal Department has issued [[a litigation hold notice]] covering all correspondence relating to the Employee.

everyday.ex: Tell his manager to [[keep everything]] - emails, chat messages, the lot.

note_fr: Notion issue de la procédure américaine, reprise par les groupes internationaux. « Hold » signifie ici gel, et non retenue. La destruction de preuves se dit « spoliation of evidence » aux États-Unis. En France, pensez à articuler cette exigence avec les durées de conservation des données personnelles.

def: A signed written account by a person of the facts he or she has personally witnessed, produced as evidence.

formal.ex: The Company relies on the [[witness statements]] of two colleagues who were present at the meeting.
formal.ex_us: The Company relies on the [[sworn declarations]] of two colleagues who were present at the meeting.

everyday.ex: Would his team leader be willing to write a [[statement]] for us?

collocations: a statement in support of the claim
note_fr: « Attestation » existe en anglais mais ne s'emploie pas dans ce sens ; « certificate » non plus. Aux États-Unis, on parle de « declaration » ou d'« affidavit » (déclaration faite sous serment). Différence pratique : en France, l'attestation écrite remplace le plus souvent l'audition du témoin ; au Royaume-Uni, l'auteur du « witness statement » vient en principe le confirmer à l'audience et répondre aux questions.

def: To tell a court or tribunal, as a witness, what one knows about the facts.

formal.ex: The Claimant's former manager [[gave evidence]] on behalf of the Respondent.
formal.ex_us: The Plaintiff's former manager [[testified]] on behalf of the Defendant.

everyday.ex: Nobody in the team wants to [[be a witness]] against a colleague.

note_fr: « To witness » signifie « être témoin de » (un fait) et non déposer en justice. « To testify » est surtout américain ; le Britannique dit « to give evidence ». « Sous serment » = « under oath » ou « on oath ». Devant le conseil de prud'hommes, l'audition de témoins à l'audience est rare.

def: The questioning of a witness by the lawyer for the opposing party, in order to test or weaken his or her evidence.

formal.ex: Counsel for the Claimant [[cross-examined]] the HR Manager for over two hours.

everyday.ex: If you give a statement in a UK case, expect to [[be cross-examined]] on every line of it.

informal.ex: She [[was grilled]] for a whole afternoon about one email.

note_fr: Technique centrale des procès de common law, sans équivalent dans la pratique prud'homale française, où les avocats plaident sur pièces. L'interrogatoire par son propre avocat s'appelle « examination-in-chief » (UK) ou « direct examination » (US). Prévenez un manager français appelé à témoigner à Londres ou à New York : l'exercice est éprouvant.

def: Evidence of what a witness was told by someone else rather than what he or she saw or heard directly.

formal.ex: The statement amounts to [[hearsay evidence]] and should be given little weight.

everyday.ex: That's all [[second-hand]] - she wasn't in the room when it happened.

note_fr: Aux États-Unis, le « hearsay » est en principe irrecevable devant un tribunal, sous réserve de nombreuses exceptions ; devant l'Employment Tribunal britannique, il est admis mais pèse peu. En France, une attestation doit relater des faits personnellement constatés : l'argument se formule donc de façon très proche.

def: Evidence that a court is allowed to take into account when deciding the case.

formal.ex: A recording made without the other person's knowledge is not necessarily [[admissible in evidence]].

everyday.ex: Will the screenshots [[be allowed as evidence]], given how she got hold of them?

collocations: to admit a document in evidence
note_fr: « Receivable » est un terme comptable (créances) : dites « admissible ». Le contraire est « inadmissible ». Retenez la nuance à expliquer à un client étranger : en France, une preuve obtenue de manière déloyale n'est pas automatiquement écartée ; le juge met en balance le droit à la preuve et les droits de l'autre partie.

def: The obligation on a party to prove the facts it relies on, failing which it loses on that point.

formal.uk: the burden of proof lies with
formal.us: the burden of proof lies with
formal.ex: Where gross misconduct is alleged, [[the burden of proof lies with]] the employer.

everyday.uk: it's up to someone to prove
everyday.us: it's up to someone to prove
everyday.ex: Here [[it's up to us to prove]] the misconduct, not up to him to disprove it.

collocations: to bear the burden of proof
to discharge the burden of proof
the burden is on the employer
note_fr: Ne dites pas « charge of the proof ». Verbes associés : « to bear » (supporter), « to discharge » ou « to meet » (s'en acquitter). Synonyme soutenu : « the onus ». En droit français, la charge varie selon la demande : elle pèse sur l'employeur pour la faute grave, elle est partagée pour la cause réelle et sérieuse et pour les heures supplémentaires.

fr: aménagement de la charge de la preuve
def: A rule under which, once the claimant has shown facts suggesting a breach, it is for the other party to prove that there was none.

formal.uk: the burden of proof shifts to
formal.us: the burden of proof shifts to
formal.ex: Once the employee has established facts from which discrimination may be presumed, [[the burden of proof shifts to]] the employer.

everyday.uk: it's then for someone to show
everyday.us: it's then for someone to show
everyday.ex: She only has to raise a plausible case; [[it's then for us to show]] there was an objective reason.

collocations: to establish a prima facie case
a reversal of the burden of proof
note_fr: « Aménagement » ne se traduit pas par « arrangement » : l'anglais dit que la charge « shifts » (se déplace). « Prima facie case » = commencement de preuve suffisant. Le mécanisme, d'origine européenne, existe aussi au Royaume-Uni en matière de discrimination ; les tribunaux américains appliquent un raisonnement en étapes comparable.

def: How convincing the evidence must be for a court to treat a fact as proved.

formal.us: by a preponderance of the evidence
formal.ex: The tribunal must be satisfied [[on the balance of probabilities]] that the conduct occurred.
formal.ex_us: The court must be satisfied [[by a preponderance of the evidence]] that the conduct occurred.

everyday.ex: We don't need certainty - we need to show it's [[more likely than not]] that he did it.

note_fr: Ne confondez pas « burden » (qui doit prouver) et « standard » (jusqu'à quel degré). En matière civile et sociale, les pays de common law se contentent de la probabilité prépondérante ; « beyond reasonable doubt » est réservé au pénal. Le droit français ne chiffre pas ce seuil : le juge forme sa conviction au vu des éléments produits.

term.uk: the employee gets the benefit of the doubt
term.us: the employee gets the benefit of the doubt

ipa.uk: /ði ɪmˌplɔɪˈiː ɡets ðə ˌbenɪfɪt əv ðə ˈdaʊt/
ipa.us: /ði ɪmˌplɔɪˈiː ɡets ðə ˌbenəfɪt əv ðə ˈdaʊt/

def: A French rule under which, if the judges remain uncertain whether a dismissal was justified, they must decide in the employee's favour.

formal.uk: any doubt shall be resolved in favour of the employee
formal.us: any doubt shall be resolved in favor of the employee
formal.ex: Under the Labour Code, where the evidence is inconclusive, [[any doubt shall be resolved in favour of the employee]].
formal.ex_us: Under the Labor Code, where the evidence is inconclusive, [[any doubt shall be resolved in favor of the employee]].

everyday.uk: the employee gets the benefit of the doubt
everyday.us: the employee gets the benefit of the doubt
everyday.ex: If it's our word against his, [[the employee gets the benefit of the doubt]] - that's the rule here.

collocations: to give someone the benefit of the doubt
to resolve a doubt in someone's favour
note_fr: Évitez le calque « the doubt profits the employee ». L'expression idiomatique est « to give someone the benefit of the doubt ». C'est une règle légale française propre au licenciement ; elle n'a pas d'équivalent au Royaume-Uni ni aux États-Unis, où celui qui supporte la charge de la preuve perd simplement s'il ne convainc pas.

explain.written: French law provides that, where the judges are left in doubt as to whether the grounds for dismissal are real and serious, that doubt must be resolved in the employee's favour.
explain.spoken: In France, if the judges can't make up their minds about whether the dismissal was justified, the employee wins. So thin evidence is the employer's problem.

def: The rule that a court may only rely on arguments and documents that each party has had a proper opportunity to see and answer.

formal.uk: the right of each party to be heard
formal.us: the right of each party to be heard
formal.ex: Exhibits disclosed on the eve of the hearing may be excluded for breach of [[the right of each party to be heard]].

everyday.uk: giving the other side a chance to respond
everyday.us: giving the other side a chance to respond
everyday.ex: You can't spring a new document on them at the hearing - it's all about [[giving the other side a chance to respond]].

collocations: to have a fair opportunity to respond
to be disclosed in good time
the right to a fair hearing
note_fr: « Contradictory principle » ne veut rien dire en anglais (« contradictory » = incohérent). « Adversarial principle » est la traduction savante, mais un interlocuteur anglophone comprendra mieux « each side must have the chance to see and answer the other side's case ». Aux États-Unis, l'idée relève du « due process ».

explain.written: Under the French principle known as le contradictoire, no argument or document may be taken into account by the court unless it has been communicated to the other party in sufficient time for that party to respond.
explain.spoken: The basic rule is that the judges can't look at anything the other side hasn't seen and had time to answer - which is why late documents get thrown out.

def: The rule that confidential communications between a lawyer and a client cannot be disclosed to the other party or to the court.

formal.uk: to be subject to legal professional privilege
formal.us: to be protected by attorney-client privilege
formal.ex: This advice [[is subject to legal professional privilege]] and must not be forwarded outside the HR leadership team.
formal.ex_us: This advice [[is protected by attorney-client privilege]] and must not be forwarded outside the HR leadership team.

everyday.ex: Anything you send the lawyers [[is privileged]]; your emails to the line manager aren't.

note_fr: « Privilege » n'a ici rien d'un avantage : c'est une protection contre la divulgation. Dans les systèmes à « disclosure » ou « discovery », elle est vitale, d'où la mention « Privileged and confidential » en tête des courriels. Un avis rédigé par un consultant RH non avocat n'est en principe pas couvert : à signaler à vos clients anglo-saxons.

def: The formal decision of a court or tribunal on a case.

formal.ex: By a [[judgment]] of 14 November, the tribunal held that the dismissal was without real and serious cause.

everyday.ex: We should get the [[ruling]] in about two months.

collocations: a judgment in favour of the employee
note_fr: Dans son sens juridique, le mot s'écrit « judgment », sans e, y compris au Royaume-Uni. « Sentence » est une peine pénale, jamais une décision prud'homale. Un « arrêt » de cour d'appel se dit aussi « judgment » ou « decision ». Verbe usuel pour introduire ce que le juge décide : « the tribunal held that... », « the court found that... ».

term.us: to take the case under advisement

def: To end the hearing without announcing a decision, which the judges will give at a later date after discussing the case.

formal.us: to take the matter under advisement
formal.ex: At the close of the hearing, the tribunal [[reserved judgment]] until 20 January.
formal.ex_us: At the close of the hearing, the court [[took the matter under advisement]] until January 20.

everyday.ex: They never decide on the day - they'll [[give their decision later]], usually within a couple of months.

note_fr: « Délibéré » ne se rend pas par « deliberate », qui comme adjectif signifie « intentionnel ». Le verbe « to deliberate » existe (« the judges are deliberating ») mais la formule technique est « to reserve judgment ». Pour annoncer une date à un client : « judgment is expected on 20 January ».

def: To make a court's decision known officially to the parties.

formal.ex: The Court of Appeal [[handed down judgment]] on 6 June.
formal.ex_us: The Court of Appeals [[entered judgment]] on June 6.

everyday.ex: The tribunal [[gave its decision]] yesterday, and it isn't good news.
everyday.ex_us: The court [[ruled]] yesterday, and it isn't good news.

note_fr: On ne dit pas « to render a judgment » en anglais britannique courant (la tournure existe en anglais juridique américain). « To pronounce » est rare. Retenez « to rule in favour of / against someone » et « to find for / against », très idiomatiques pour dire qui a gagné.

def: The final part of a judgment, which states exactly what the court orders, as opposed to the reasoning that leads to it.

formal.uk: the operative part of the judgment
formal.us: the operative part of the judgment
formal.ex: Only [[the operative part of the judgment]] is binding on the parties and capable of enforcement.

everyday.ex: Skip the reasoning for now and look at [[what the court actually ordered]] on the last page.

collocations: the order made by the court
note_fr: « Dispositive » est un faux ami partiel : aux États-Unis, « a dispositive motion » est une requête qui met fin au litige. Les motifs se disent « the reasons » ou « the reasoning » (pas « the motivations »). Pour un client, le plus clair reste « the order at the end of the judgment ».

def: To decide that a claim fails and that the claimant will not obtain what was asked for.

formal.ex: The tribunal [[dismissed the claims]] in their entirety and ordered the Claimant to pay the costs.

everyday.ex: The judges [[rejected the claim]] for overtime but accepted the one about the bonus.

informal.ex: The whole thing was [[thrown out]] in under an hour.

note_fr: Double sens à maîtriser : « to dismiss an employee » = licencier, « to dismiss a claim » = rejeter une demande. « The claim failed » est la tournure la plus naturelle à l'oral. Aux États-Unis, « dismissed with prejudice » signifie que la demande ne pourra plus être réintroduite.

def: To decide, as a court, that a party must pay a sum of money to the other party.

formal.ex: The Company [[was ordered to pay]] the Employee the equivalent of six months' salary.

everyday.ex: Worst case, we [[have to pay]] him about forty thousand euros.

collocations: to order the employer to pay damages
to award the claimant a sum
note_fr: Faux amis : « to condemn » exprime une réprobation morale et « to sentence » une peine pénale. En matière civile, on dit « the court ordered the company to pay... » ou « awarded the employee... ». « To be found liable » = voir sa responsabilité retenue ; « guilty » est réservé au pénal.

def: To obtain a decision in one's favour from a court or tribunal.

formal.ex: The Employee [[succeeded in her claim]] for unpaid overtime but not in her claim for unfair dismissal.
formal.ex_us: The Employee [[prevailed on her claim]] for unpaid overtime but not on her claim for wrongful termination.

everyday.ex: Even if we [[win the case]], we won't get our legal fees back.

note_fr: « To gain the case » est un calque : on « wins » ou « loses » a case. La partie gagnante est « the successful party » (UK) ou « the prevailing party » (US) ; la partie perdante, « the unsuccessful / losing party ». Gagner en partie : « to succeed in part ».

def: To ask a court or tribunal to decide that a dismissal was unlawful or unjustified.

formal.ex: The Employee has twelve months in which to [[contest the dismissal]] before the employment tribunal.
formal.ex_us: The Employee has twelve months in which to [[contest the termination]] before the labor court.

everyday.ex: We should assume he'll [[challenge the dismissal]] and prepare the file accordingly.
everyday.ex_us: We should assume he'll [[challenge the termination]] and prepare the file accordingly.

collocations: to dispute the grounds for dismissal
note_fr: Le verbe le plus naturel est « to challenge ». Notez les étiquettes nationales : « unfair dismissal » au Royaume-Uni, « wrongful termination » ou « wrongful discharge » aux États-Unis. Attention : en droit anglais, « wrongful dismissal » désigne seulement la rupture sans respect du préavis contractuel.

def: Money that a court orders one party to pay to another to make up for a loss or a wrong.

formal.ex: The tribunal awarded the Employee [[damages]] for dismissal without real and serious cause.

everyday.ex: How much [[compensation]] is she likely to get?
everyday.ex_us: How much in [[damages]] is she likely to get?

note_fr: « Damages » (toujours au pluriel, verbe au pluriel) = dommages-intérêts ; « damage » (indénombrable) = dégâts. N'ajoutez pas « and interests ». Au Royaume-Uni, l'Employment Tribunal parle de « compensation » ; aux États-Unis, « compensation » désigne d'abord la rémunération, d'où un risque de malentendu.

def: The sum of money that a court, tribunal or arbitrator decides a party should receive.

formal.ex: [[The award]] is expressed as a gross amount and is subject to social security contributions where applicable.

everyday.ex: [[The payout]] could be anything between three and ten months' salary.

collocations: to award someone six months' pay
note_fr: « Award » est aussi un verbe : « the tribunal awarded her 20,000 euros ». Le mot désigne par ailleurs un prix ou une récompense, et, en arbitrage, la sentence elle-même. Ne dites pas « indemnity » pour une somme allouée par le juge : en anglais, « indemnity » est une garantie contractuelle contre un risque.

fr: barème d'indemnisation du licenciement sans cause réelle et sérieuse
def: The French statutory table that fixes, according to length of service, the minimum and maximum damages a court may award for an unjustified dismissal.

formal.uk: the statutory scale of damages for unfair dismissal
formal.us: the statutory scale of damages for wrongful termination
formal.ex: Compensation is assessed by reference to [[the statutory scale of damages for unfair dismissal]], which depends on the employee's length of service.
formal.ex_us: Compensation is assessed by reference to [[the statutory scale of damages for wrongful termination]], which depends on the employee's length of service.

everyday.ex: With four years' service, [[the compensation scale]] gives us a fairly narrow range.
everyday.ex_us: With four years of service, [[the damages scale]] gives us a fairly narrow range.

collocations: the upper limit of the scale
the scale does not apply to
note_fr: Souvent appelé « barème Macron » : dites « the so-called Macron scale » et expliquez. « Barème » ne se traduit ni par « barometer » ni par « schedule » seul. Point essentiel pour un client étranger : le barème rend le risque prévisible, mais il est écarté lorsque le licenciement est nul (harcèlement, discrimination, atteinte à une liberté fondamentale).

explain.written: French law lays down a mandatory scale which sets, by reference to the employee's length of service and expressed in months of gross salary, the minimum and maximum damages that a court may award for a dismissal without real and serious cause.
explain.spoken: There's a legal scale in France: depending on how long the person has worked for you, the judges have to stay between a minimum and a maximum number of months' salary. It makes the risk fairly easy to budget for.

def: To set a maximum amount that a court is allowed to award.

formal.uk: to be subject to a statutory cap
formal.us: to be subject to a statutory cap
formal.ex: Damages for dismissal without real and serious cause [[are subject to a statutory cap]] expressed in months of salary.

everyday.ex: The good news is that the damages [[are capped]], so we know our maximum exposure.

note_fr: « Plafond » = « cap » ou « ceiling » ; « plancher » = « floor ». « To plafond » n'existe pas et « to limit » est moins précis. « Uncapped » (sans plafond) est très utile pour signaler les demandes qui échappent au barème. Le droit britannique connaît lui aussi des plafonds légaux d'indemnisation, dont le régime évolue : vérifiez la règle en vigueur.

def: The harm, financial or otherwise, that a person has suffered and for which compensation is claimed.

formal.ex: It is for the Employee to demonstrate the extent of [[the loss suffered]] as a result of the breach.
formal.ex_us: It is for the Employee to demonstrate the extent of [[the harm suffered]] as a result of the breach.

everyday.ex: The judges want to see [[what she has actually lost]] - how long she was out of work, for instance.

note_fr: Faux ami : « prejudice » signifie préjugé (ou, dans « without prejudice », réserve de droits). Le préjudice se dit « loss », « harm » ou « damage » (au singulier). Le préjudice moral se rend par « non-financial loss », « injury to feelings » (UK, surtout en matière de discrimination) ou « emotional distress » (US).

def: To take reasonable steps to reduce the harm one has suffered, for example by looking for a new job after a dismissal.

formal.ex: Compensation may be reduced where the Claimant has failed to comply with [[the duty to mitigate]].

everyday.ex: In the UK she'd be expected to [[mitigate her loss]] by looking for another job.
everyday.ex_us: In the US she'd be expected to [[mitigate her damages]] by looking for another job.

collocations: to take reasonable steps to find work
note_fr: Règle de common law : le salarié britannique ou américain doit prouver ses recherches d'emploi, faute de quoi son indemnisation est réduite. Le droit français ne connaît pas d'obligation générale de minimiser son dommage, même si le juge tient compte de la situation du salarié après la rupture. Ne confondez pas « mitigate » (atténuer) et « militate » (militer en faveur de).

def: A court order, or a decision, that a dismissed employee must be given his or her job back.

formal.ex: Where the dismissal is void, the court may [[order reinstatement]] at the employee's request.

everyday.ex: Does she actually want to [[get her job back]], or is she after compensation?

note_fr: « Reintegration » évoque la réinsertion sociale : le terme juridique est « reinstatement » (verbe « to reinstate »). Au Royaume-Uni, on distingue « reinstatement » (même poste) et « re-engagement » (poste comparable). En France, la réintégration est surtout de droit en cas de nullité du licenciement ; elle reste exceptionnelle en pratique dans les trois pays.

def: Wages that should have been paid in the past and that the employer is ordered, or agrees, to pay now.

formal.ex: The Company was ordered to pay [[arrears of salary]] for the period from January to June.
formal.ex_us: The Company was ordered to pay [[back wages]] for the period from January through June.

everyday.ex: He's claiming three years' [[back pay]] for overtime nobody ever recorded.

note_fr: Ne dites pas « salary reminder » ni « recall of salary ». « Arrears » est toujours au pluriel ; « to be in arrears » = avoir du retard de paiement. Aux États-Unis, « front pay » désigne à l'inverse l'indemnisation des salaires futurs perdus lorsque la réintégration n'est pas possible.

fr: résiliation judiciaire du contrat de travail
def: Under French law, the ending of an employment contract by a court, at the request of an employee who complains of serious breaches by the employer.

formal.uk: to apply for judicial termination of the contract
formal.us: to apply for judicial termination of the contract
formal.ex: While remaining in post, the Employee [[applied for judicial termination of the contract]] on the ground of repeated non-payment of overtime.

everyday.uk: to ask the court to end the contract
everyday.us: to ask the court to end the contract
everyday.ex: She hasn't resigned - she's [[asked the court to end the contract]] and put the blame on us.

collocations: on the ground of the employer's breaches
to remain in employment pending the decision
to take effect as an unfair dismissal
note_fr: Notion française. L'analogie la plus parlante pour un Britannique ou un Américain est le « constructive dismissal » (« constructive discharge » aux États-Unis), à cette différence près que le salarié français reste en poste jusqu'à la décision du juge. « Resiliation » n'existe pas en anglais.

explain.written: French law allows an employee who remains in post to ask the employment tribunal to terminate the contract on account of sufficiently serious breaches by the employer; if the claim succeeds, the termination takes effect as a dismissal without real and serious cause.
explain.spoken: It's a bit like constructive dismissal, except she stays in her job and asks the court to end the contract because of what the employer has done. If she wins, it counts as an unfair dismissal.

def: A fast court procedure for obtaining a temporary order in urgent or obvious cases, without a full decision on the merits.

formal.ex: The Employee made [[an application for interim relief]] seeking payment of three months' unpaid salary.
formal.ex_us: The Employee filed [[a motion for preliminary relief]] seeking payment of three months of unpaid salary.

everyday.ex: For unpaid wages he'll use [[the fast-track procedure]] - he could have an order in a few weeks.

collocations: to apply for an interim order
pending a decision on the merits
note_fr: « Referee » est un arbitre sportif : faux ami. « Summary proceedings » est une autre traduction courante. Le référé prud'homal permet notamment d'obtenir rapidement des salaires impayés ou des documents de fin de contrat. Ne le confondez pas avec l'« interim relief » britannique au sens strict, qui est un recours très spécifique ouvert dans certains cas de licenciement.

explain.written: The référé is an expedited procedure before a special panel of the employment tribunal, which may order urgent or provisional measures, or an interim payment where the obligation cannot seriously be disputed, without ruling on the merits of the dispute.
explain.spoken: There's a fast-track procedure for urgent or clear-cut matters, like unpaid wages. You get a provisional order in a few weeks, and the main case can still be heard later.

def: A sum that a court orders a party to pay on account, before the final decision, because the debt is not seriously open to dispute.

formal.uk: an interim payment on account of
formal.us: an interim payment on account of
formal.ex: The judge ordered the Company to make [[an interim payment on account of]] the unpaid commission.

everyday.ex: He's asking the judge for [[a payment up front]] while the main case goes on.

note_fr: Faux ami comptable : « a provision » est une somme mise de côté dans les comptes en prévision d'un risque (voir « to make a provision for a claim »), et jamais une somme versée à l'adversaire. « On account » = à titre d'acompte, à valoir.

def: A sum fixed by a court that a party must pay for each day or week of delay in complying with an order.

formal.uk: subject to a penalty of ... per day of delay
formal.us: subject to a penalty of ... per day of delay
formal.ex: The Company shall deliver the amended payslips within fifteen days, [[subject to a penalty of fifty euros per day of delay]].

everyday.ex: If we don't send the certificate on time, there's [[a daily fine]] until we do.

collocations: to comply with the order in time
note_fr: Double piège : en droit du travail, « astreinte » désigne aussi la période où le salarié doit rester joignable (« on-call duty ») ; ici, il s'agit de la pénalité prononcée par le juge. Le mécanisme n'existe pas tel quel en common law, où le non-respect d'une ordonnance est sanctionné par le « contempt of court ».

explain.written: An astreinte is a financial penalty, fixed by the court at a given amount per day or other period of delay, intended to compel a party to comply with an order such as the delivery of documents.
explain.spoken: The court can add a daily penalty to its order - so much per day until you hand over the documents. It's there to make sure the order is actually obeyed.

def: The rule or order under which a judgment must be complied with immediately, even though an appeal has been lodged.

formal.ex: The award of unpaid salary [[is provisionally enforceable]] notwithstanding any appeal.

everyday.uk: to have to pay straight away
everyday.us: to have to pay right away
everyday.ex: On the wages, we [[have to pay straight away]], appeal or no appeal.
everyday.ex_us: On the wages, we [[have to pay right away]], appeal or no appeal.

collocations: pending the outcome of the appeal
note_fr: Ne dites pas « provisional execution » : « execution » évoque d'abord la peine de mort ou la signature d'un acte. Le mécanisme inverse est le « stay of enforcement » (suspension de l'exécution). En droit prud'homal, certaines condamnations, notamment salariales, sont exécutoires de plein droit ; pour les autres, tout dépend de ce que le jugement ordonne.

explain.written: In French procedure, exécution provisoire means that a first-instance judgment, or part of it, must be complied with at once even if it is appealed; before the employment tribunal, it attaches automatically to certain awards and may be ordered for others.
explain.spoken: Appealing doesn't always stop the clock: some parts of the judgment, wages in particular, have to be paid immediately, and you get the money back only if you win on appeal.

def: Damages awarded not to compensate the victim's loss but to punish the wrongdoer and deter others.

formal.ex: French law does not provide for [[exemplary damages]]; compensation is limited to the loss actually suffered.
formal.ex_us: French law does not provide for [[punitive damages]]; compensation is limited to the loss actually suffered.

everyday.ex: Tell head office not to expect American-style [[punitive damages]] here - they simply don't exist.

note_fr: En France, le principe est la réparation intégrale du préjudice, sans plus : pas de dommages-intérêts punitifs. Le terme britannique est « exemplary damages », rarissimes en matière d'emploi. Aux États-Unis, ils sont possibles dans certains contentieux, parfois dans la limite de plafonds légaux, ce qui explique en partie les montants élevés dont vos clients ont l'habitude.

def: A claim brought with no real basis, or for an improper purpose such as harassing the other party.

formal.ex: The Company counterclaimed for damages on the ground that the proceedings constituted [[an abuse of process]].

everyday.ex: However weak it looks, the judges will rarely treat it as [[a vexatious claim]].
everyday.ex_us: However weak it looks, the judges will rarely treat it as [[a frivolous lawsuit]].

informal.ex: Frankly, it's [[a try-on]] - he's hoping we'll pay him to go away.
informal.ex_us: Frankly, it's [[a shakedown]] - he's hoping we'll pay him to go away.

collocations: a claim with no reasonable prospect of success
note_fr: « Abusive » en anglais signifie injurieux ou maltraitant (« abusive language », « an abusive manager ») : « abusive procedure » serait un contresens. « Nuisance claim » désigne la demande de faible valeur que l'on règle pour avoir la paix. Rappelez au client que les juges français admettent très rarement le caractère abusif d'une action.

def: To decide, as a claimant, to stop the proceedings one has started.

formal.ex: In consideration of the payment, the Employee undertakes to [[withdraw the claim]] within eight days.
formal.ex_us: In consideration of the payment, the Employee undertakes to [[voluntarily dismiss the claim]] within eight days.

everyday.ex: If we pay the bonus, will she [[drop the case]]?

collocations: to abandon part of the claim
note_fr: « To desist » signifie cesser de faire quelque chose (« cease and desist ») et ne s'emploie pas pour un désistement d'instance. Aux États-Unis, c'est le demandeur lui-même qui « dismisses » sa propre action (« voluntary dismissal ») : ne le confondez pas avec le rejet par le juge.

def: To end a dispute by agreement between the parties before the court gives its decision.

formal.ex: The parties [[reached a settlement]] shortly before the hearing and the claim was withdrawn.

everyday.ex: My instinct is to [[settle]] now rather than wait two years for a judgment.

informal.ex: Their lawyer rang yesterday - I think they want to [[do a deal]].
informal.ex_us: Their lawyer called yesterday - I think they want to [[cut a deal]].

collocations: to settle at the door of the court
to settle for six months' salary
note_fr: « To transact » signifie conclure une opération commerciale : n'employez pas ce verbe. « To settle for » + montant ; « to settle with » + personne. « At the door of the court » (UK) ou « on the courthouse steps » (US) : transiger juste avant l'audience. « To compromise a claim » existe en anglais juridique britannique, mais « compromise » seul évoque plutôt une concession.

fr: radiation de l'affaire / rejet pour défaut de diligence

term.us: to dismiss for failure to prosecute

def: To remove a case from the court's list, or put an end to it, because a party has not taken the steps required of it.

formal.us: to be dismissed for failure to prosecute
formal.ex: The claim [[was struck out]] on the ground that the Claimant had repeatedly failed to comply with the tribunal's orders.
formal.ex_us: The claim [[was dismissed for failure to prosecute]] on the ground that the Plaintiff had repeatedly failed to comply with the court's orders.

everyday.uk: to be taken off the list
everyday.us: to be taken off the docket
everyday.ex: If his lawyer doesn't file anything by June, the case will [[be taken off the list]].
everyday.ex_us: If his lawyer doesn't file anything by June, the case will [[be taken off the docket]].

collocations: to restore the case to the list
note_fr: Attention à la portée : la radiation française est une mesure d'administration qui suspend l'affaire, laquelle peut être rétablie ; le « strike-out » britannique met fin à la demande. Précisez donc « removed from the list, but it can be restored ». « Radiation » en anglais ne désigne que le rayonnement.

def: To ask a higher court to review and change the decision of a lower court.

formal.ex: The Company [[lodged an appeal against]] the judgment within the one-month time limit.
formal.ex_us: The Company [[filed an appeal from]] the judgment within the one-month deadline.

everyday.ex: If we lose, do we [[appeal against]] the decision or cut our losses?
everyday.ex_us: If we lose, do we [[appeal]] the decision or cut our losses?

note_fr: Différence de construction : le Britannique dit « to appeal against a decision », l'Américain « to appeal a decision » (transitif direct). « To make appeal » est un calque. « To call » ne convient jamais. L'appelant est « the appellant », l'intimé « the respondent » (US : « the appellee »).

def: The court that re-examines a case decided by a lower court when one of the parties challenges the decision.

formal.ex: The judgment was upheld by the employment division of [[the Court of Appeal]].
formal.ex_us: The judgment was affirmed by the employment division of [[the Court of Appeals]].

everyday.ex: [[The appeal court]] looks at everything again, the facts as well as the law.
everyday.ex_us: [[The appeals court]] looks at everything again, the facts as well as the law.

collocations: to go to the Court of Appeal
note_fr: Notez le s américain : « Court of Appeals ». Différence de fond à expliquer : la cour d'appel française rejuge l'affaire en fait et en droit, alors que l'Employment Appeal Tribunal britannique et les cours d'appel américaines contrôlent pour l'essentiel les erreurs de droit. Un client anglo-saxon sous-estime donc souvent la portée d'un appel en France.

def: The highest French court for civil, commercial, employment and criminal cases, which reviews whether the law was correctly applied.

formal.uk: the Cour de cassation (French Supreme Court)
formal.us: the Cour de cassation (French Supreme Court)
formal.ex: The employment division of [[the Cour de cassation (French Supreme Court)]] has consistently held that such a clause is unenforceable.

everyday.ex: [[The French Supreme Court]] ruled on exactly this point a couple of years ago.

collocations: the employment division of the Supreme Court
to take the case to the Supreme Court
note_fr: Gardez le nom français à l'écrit et ajoutez une glose. N'écrivez pas « Court of Cassation » sans explication à un lecteur anglo-saxon. La « chambre sociale » se rend par « the employment division ». Contrairement à la Cour suprême des États-Unis, elle ne contrôle pas la constitutionnalité des lois et rend plusieurs milliers de décisions par an.

explain.written: The Cour de cassation is the highest court in the French judicial system; it does not retry the facts but reviews whether the lower courts have correctly applied the law, and its employment division shapes much of French employment case law.
explain.spoken: It's our supreme court for this kind of case. It doesn't look at the facts again - it only checks that the court of appeal applied the law properly.

term.uk: appeal on a point of law
term.us: appeal on a point of law

def: A final appeal to the highest court, limited to arguing that the lower court made a legal error.

formal.uk: to lodge an appeal on a point of law with
formal.us: to file an appeal on a point of law with
formal.ex: The Employee [[lodged an appeal on a point of law with]] the Cour de cassation.
formal.ex_us: The Employee [[filed an appeal on a point of law with]] the Cour de cassation.

everyday.uk: to take it to the Supreme Court
everyday.us: to take it to the Supreme Court
everyday.ex: They could [[take it to the Supreme Court]], but only on the law, and it won't stop them having to pay.

collocations: on a point of law only
to exhaust all avenues of appeal
note_fr: « Pourvoi » n'a pas d'équivalent en un mot. « Cassation » employé seul est incompris. Aux États-Unis, la voie comparable devant la Cour suprême est la « petition for certiorari », accordée de manière discrétionnaire. Point pratique : le pourvoi n'est en principe pas suspensif, ce qu'un client étranger ignore presque toujours.

explain.written: A pourvoi en cassation is an appeal to the Cour de cassation which may be based only on errors of law or procedure in the decision under challenge; the court does not re-examine the facts.
explain.spoken: After the court of appeal, the only option left is an appeal to the supreme court, and only on points of law. They won't look at the facts again.

def: To decide, as a higher court, that the lower court's decision stands, or on the contrary that it must be changed.

formal.ex: The Court of Appeal [[upheld the judgment]] in so far as it found the dismissal unjustified, but set it aside as to the amount of damages.
formal.ex_us: The Court of Appeals [[affirmed the judgment]] insofar as it found the termination unjustified, but reversed it as to the amount of damages.

everyday.ex: The appeal court [[overturned the decision]], so we're back to owing nothing.
everyday.ex_us: The appeals court [[reversed the decision]], so we're back to owing nothing.

note_fr: « To confirm » se comprend mais le verbe juridique est « to uphold » (UK) ou « to affirm » (US). Pour « infirmer » : « to overturn », « to set aside », « to reverse » ; « to infirm » n'existe pas. Au Royaume-Uni, on dit aussi que la cour « allows the appeal » (y fait droit) ou « dismisses the appeal » (le rejette).

def: To cancel a lower court's decision and send the case back to another court to be decided again.

formal.uk: to quash the decision and remit the case to
formal.us: to vacate the decision and remand the case to
formal.ex: The Cour de cassation [[quashed the decision and remitted the case to]] a different court of appeal.
formal.ex_us: The Cour de cassation [[vacated the decision and remanded the case to]] a different court of appeals.

everyday.ex: The Supreme Court has [[sent the case back]] to be heard again, so we're not done yet.

collocations: to remit the case for rehearing
to be remanded for a new trial
note_fr: « To break a judgment » est un calque à proscrire. « To quash » (UK) et « to vacate » (US) = annuler ; « to remit » (UK) et « to remand » (US) = renvoyer devant une juridiction. Au Royaume-Uni, « to remand » appartient au pénal (détention provisoire) : ne l'employez pas pour un renvoi civil.

def: The body of rules that results from the decisions of the courts, as opposed to legislation.

formal.ex: It is [[settled case law]] that a non-compete clause without financial compensation is void.

everyday.ex: The statute is silent on this, so it all comes down to [[what the courts have said]].

note_fr: Faux ami : « jurisprudence » en anglais désigne la philosophie ou la théorie du droit. « Case law » est indénombrable : pour une décision, dites « a case », « a ruling », « a decision ». Un revirement se dit « a reversal of the case law » ou « a departure from previous decisions ». Le précédent n'est pas formellement obligatoire en France, contrairement aux pays de common law.

def: A court decision that can no longer be challenged by an ordinary appeal.

formal.ex: Once the time limit for appeal has expired, the judgment becomes [[final and binding]].

everyday.ex: It's not [[final]] yet - they've still got three weeks to appeal.

collocations: to exhaust all rights of appeal
note_fr: Faux ami : « definitive » signifie « qui fait autorité, de référence » (« the definitive guide ») ; pour une décision de justice, dites « final ». « Final and binding » est le doublet consacré. Dans un calendrier, précisez « final, subject to appeal » tant que le délai court.

def: The rule that a matter finally decided by a court cannot be brought before the courts again by the same parties.

formal.uk: to be barred by res judicata
formal.us: to be barred by res judicata
formal.ex: The new claim concerns the same dismissal and [[is barred by res judicata]].

everyday.ex: He can't bring that up again - it [[has already been decided]].

collocations: a final decision on the same facts
note_fr: L'anglais juridique garde l'expression latine ; « authority of the judged thing » n'existe pas. Aux États-Unis, on parle aussi de « claim preclusion ». À l'oral, préférez une paraphrase : « it has already been decided and can't be reopened ». « To relitigate » = replaider.

def: To decide, as a court, that it does not have the power to hear a particular case, which must go to another court.

formal.uk: to decline jurisdiction in favour of
formal.us: to decline jurisdiction in favor of
formal.ex: The employment tribunal [[declined jurisdiction in favour of]] the commercial court on the ground that the Claimant was a company officer and not an employee.
formal.ex_us: The labor court [[declined jurisdiction in favor of]] the commercial court on the ground that the Plaintiff was a company officer and not an employee.

everyday.uk: to say it's not the right court
everyday.us: to say it's not the right court
everyday.ex: Our first argument is that the tribunal should [[say it's not the right court]], because he was never an employee.

collocations: to have jurisdiction over a dispute
note_fr: Faux ami redoutable : « incompetent » signifie incapable, nul dans son travail. Dire « the tribunal is incompetent » ferait sourire ; dites « the tribunal has no jurisdiction » ou « lacks jurisdiction ». L'exception d'incompétence se dit « a challenge to jurisdiction » ou « a jurisdictional objection ».

def: The money a party spends on a court case, mainly on its lawyers.

formal.us: to bear one's own attorney's fees
formal.ex: Each party shall [[bear its own costs]].
formal.ex_us: Each party shall [[bear its own attorney's fees]].

everyday.ex: Even if we win, the [[legal costs]] will run to five figures.
everyday.ex_us: Even if we win, the [[legal fees]] will run to five figures.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, « costs » (pluriel) désigne tous les frais du procès, honoraires compris ; aux États-Unis, « costs » ne vise que les frais de greffe et assimilés, les honoraires étant les « attorney's fees ». Devant les tribunaux civils anglais, le perdant paie en principe les frais du gagnant, mais pas devant l'Employment Tribunal, où chacun garde normalement les siens ; aux États-Unis, chacun paie son avocat, sauf loi contraire.

def: An arrangement under which the lawyer is paid, wholly or partly, only if the client wins or obtains a settlement.

formal.ex: The Claimant's solicitors are acting under [[a conditional fee agreement]].
formal.ex_us: The Plaintiff's attorneys are acting under [[a contingency fee agreement]].

everyday.uk: on a no win, no fee basis
everyday.ex: His lawyer is working [[on a no win, no fee basis]], so he has nothing to lose by going on.
everyday.ex_us: His lawyer is working [[on contingency]], so he has nothing to lose by going on.

collocations: to take a case on contingency
note_fr: Aux États-Unis, l'avocat du salarié travaille très souvent au pourcentage (« on contingency »), ce qui facilite l'accès au juge. En France, l'honoraire fixé uniquement en fonction du résultat est interdit ; seul un honoraire complémentaire de résultat (« a success fee on top of a base fee ») est admis. Ne traduisez pas « honoraires » par « honorarium », réservé à la rétribution d'un conférencier.

fr: indemnité au titre de l'article 700 du code de procédure civile
def: A sum that a French court may order the losing party to pay towards the winning party's lawyers' fees.

formal.uk: a contribution towards the other party's legal costs
formal.us: a contribution toward the other party's legal fees
formal.ex: The Company was further ordered to pay [[a contribution towards the other party's legal costs]] under Article 700 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
formal.ex_us: The Company was further ordered to pay [[a contribution toward the other party's legal fees]] under Article 700 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

everyday.ex: If we lose, we'll also have to pay [[something towards her legal fees]] - usually a fairly modest sum.
everyday.ex_us: If we lose, we'll also have to pay [[something toward her legal fees]] - usually a fairly modest sum.

collocations: to claim a contribution to costs
to recover part of one's fees
note_fr: Notion française : la somme est fixée librement par le juge, en équité, et ne couvre généralement qu'une partie des honoraires réels. Ne laissez pas croire à un client britannique qu'il s'agit d'un « costs order » à l'anglaise (remboursement substantiel des frais), ni à un client américain qu'il s'agit d'un « fee-shifting » intégral.
